Monument-Valley.verdict: A short, gorgeous puzzle game where every level is a piece of impossible architecture you can rotate and reshape.
Monument-Valley.bestFor: Anyone who wants a calm, beautiful game they can finish in an evening or two.
pros: Optical-illusion puzzles that feel fresh even years later
Paid once, with no ads in the way
Art and sound design that make it feel like a pop-up book
cons: Short: most players finish it in a few hours
Puzzles are gentle, so experts may want more challenge
body: Monument Valley asks you to guide a small princess through buildings that could never exist in real life. Turning a crank or sliding a pillar changes how paths connect, and the game is built around that moment when an impossible staircase suddenly makes sense.

It is a premium game in the old sense: you pay once and get a complete, polished experience. It is the easiest recommendation on this site for someone who says they don't usually play games on their phone.
Monument-Valley.author: editors

Monument-Valley-2.verdict: The sequel adds a parent-and-child story and cleverer level ideas without losing what made the original special.
Monument-Valley-2.bestFor: Players who finished the first game and want more of the same magic.
pros: Puzzles build on the original's ideas in surprising ways
A touching story told almost without words
Premium: no ads and no paywalls mid-game
cons: Still short, and still on the easy side
Works best if you've played the first game
body: Monument Valley 2 follows a mother and daughter, and uses two characters to create puzzles the first game couldn't. Some levels split the pair, others ask you to move them in step.
If you liked the first game, this is an easy buy. If you've never played either, start with the original; they are both short enough to play back to back.
Monument-Valley-2.author: editors

Minecraft.verdict: The full Minecraft experience on a phone: endless building, survival and multiplayer for a one-time price.
Minecraft.bestFor: Creative players of any age, and families who want a game they can play together.
pros: Practically limitless: survival, creative and multiplayer modes
Cross-play with friends on consoles and PC
cons: Touch controls take getting used to for precise building
body: Minecraft needs little introduction. On Android you get the same world-building game as on other platforms, including survival with crafting and monsters, a creative mode with unlimited blocks, and online play with friends.

The one-time price buys years of play. Touch controls are the main compromise; a controller or a bigger screen helps. The optional marketplace sells skins and worlds, but nothing in it is needed to enjoy the game.
Minecraft.author: editors

Terraria.verdict: A 2D sandbox adventure packed with bosses, crafting and secrets that can easily last a hundred hours.
Terraria.bestFor: Players who like exploring, crafting and fighting bosses at their own pace.
pros: Huge amount of content for a single purchase
No ads and no in-app purchases
cons: Slow, confusing start without a guide
body: Terraria looks like a simple 2D game at first, but it opens into a long adventure: dig, build a base, craft better gear and take on a string of increasingly tough bosses.
The mobile version is a complete game with no ads or extra purchases. The first hour can be confusing, and a wiki helps, but few phone games offer this much for the price.
Terraria.author: editors

Geometry-Dash.verdict: A tough, rhythm-driven platformer where you tap in time with the music and fail a lot, in the best way.
Geometry-Dash.bestFor: Players who enjoy a challenge and like retrying until they get it right.
pros: Levels are synced closely to the soundtrack
cons: Very hard; frustration is part of the design
Paid upfront (there's no free full version)
body: In Geometry Dash you control a small cube that jumps, flies and flips through levels timed to the beat of each song. One mistake sends you back to the start, so you learn each level by heart.

The official levels are only the beginning: the community has built a huge number of its own. It isn't for players who want to relax, but if you like mastering something difficult it is hard to put down.
Geometry-Dash.author: editors

Bloons-TD-6.verdict: The best tower defense game on Android, with deep strategy, regular updates and no pressure to pay.
Bloons-TD-6.bestFor: Strategy fans who enjoy planning, upgrading and replaying levels on harder settings.
pros: Large variety of towers and upgrade paths
Regular free updates with new maps and events
cons: Optional purchases on top of the upfront price
body: Bloons TD 6 has you placing monkeys with darts, magic and much more to pop waves of balloons before they reach the exit. Every tower has several upgrade paths, so the same map can be won in many different ways.
It costs money upfront and also sells optional extras, but the core game is complete without them. For anyone who likes strategy it is one of the best-value games on the store.
Bloons-TD-6.author: editors

Clash-of-Clans.verdict: The classic base-builder: still polished and social, but built around long wait timers that push you to spend.
Clash-of-Clans.bestFor: Patient players who like checking in a few times a day and playing with a clan.
pros: Free to start, with plenty to do in the first weeks
cons: Upgrades take hours or days unless you pay
Later stages are slow for free players
body: Clash of Clans has you building a village, training troops and raiding other players. Planning an attack and watching it unfold is still satisfying after all these years.

The catch is time: upgrades take longer and longer, and gems speed them up. If you're happy to play a few minutes at a time over months, it's fun for free. If you want fast progress, it gets expensive.
Clash-of-Clans.author: editors

Clash-Royale.verdict: Fast, skill-based card battles that last about three minutes, with a fair amount of pay-to-progress.
Clash-Royale.bestFor: Competitive players who want quick head-to-head matches.
pros: Short matches fit a coffee break
Real skill in timing and card choice
cons: Upgrading cards is slow without spending
Can be frustrating against higher-level decks
body: Clash Royale mixes a card game with tower defense: you drop troops onto a small arena and try to destroy your opponent's towers within three minutes.
Matches are tense and skill matters, especially elixir management. Card levels also matter, though, and paying speeds those up. It's best enjoyed casually rather than as a ladder you must climb.
Clash-Royale.author: editors

Brawl-Stars.verdict: Quick, colorful team battles with lots of modes and fair matchmaking for casual players.
Brawl-Stars.bestFor: Friends who want short matches together, and anyone who likes action without a steep learning curve.
pros: Matches take two or three minutes
Many modes, from soccer to battle royale
Easy to learn, with room to improve
cons: Lots of currencies and passes to keep track of
body: Brawl Stars is a top-down team shooter where every character, or brawler, plays differently. Modes rotate often, so there's always something new to try.
It's one of the most generous Supercell games for free players, though shops and passes are everywhere. Playing with friends is where it shines.
Brawl-Stars.author: editors

Among-Us.verdict: A brilliant social deduction game with friends; less fun with strangers in public lobbies.
Among-Us.bestFor: Groups of friends who already chat together.
pros: Simple to learn, endless arguments to have
Great with a voice chat group
Plenty of free cosmetics and roles
cons: Contains ads in the free version
body: In Among Us, a crew repairs a spaceship while one or more impostors secretly sabotage it. Meetings turn into debates where everyone accuses everyone.
The game is only as good as the people you play with. With a group of friends it's one of the funniest games on a phone. With random players, results vary.
Among-Us.author: editors

Roblox.verdict: Not one game but millions, made by players, with something for every taste and a lot to keep an eye on for younger kids.
Roblox.bestFor: Kids and teens who want to play with friends, and parents willing to set up parental controls.
cons: Parents should set up controls for younger children
body: Roblox is a platform full of games made by its community: obstacle courses, role-play towns, tycoon games and much more. Most kids play it for the social side, meeting friends in shared worlds.
It's free, but Robux, the in-game currency, is spent on almost everything cosmetic. Parents should look at the account's spending limits and chat settings before handing it to a young child.
Roblox.author: editors

PUBG-MOBILE.verdict: One of the most complete battle royale games on mobile, with realistic gunplay and big maps.
PUBG-MOBILE.bestFor: Teens and adults who want serious, tactical shooter matches.
pros: Many modes beyond the classic 100-player match
Good controls with lots of settings
cons: Big download and needs a capable phone
Constant events, passes and shop offers
body: PUBG Mobile drops 100 players onto an island to scavenge for gear and fight until one squad remains. Matches are slower and more tactical than in arcade-style shooters.
It looks and plays great on a good phone, but older devices struggle. The free game is fair; the shop is mostly cosmetics, though there's a lot of it.
PUBG-MOBILE.author: editors

Free-Fire.verdict: A faster, shorter battle royale with character abilities; this listing is Free Fire MAX, the higher-detail edition.
Free-Fire.bestFor: Players who want quick battle royale matches with friends.
pros: Characters and pets add special abilities
cons: MAX edition needs more storage and a better phone than classic Free Fire
body: Free Fire matches pack 50 players onto a smaller map, so fights start quickly. Characters bring abilities, like faster healing or shields, that add a layer of strategy.
Note that the Google Play link here is for Free Fire MAX, which has improved graphics. It's a great quick-match shooter if your phone can handle it.
Free-Fire.author: editors

Stumble-Guys.verdict: Chaotic, silly party races for up to 32 players, perfect for short sessions with friends.
Stumble-Guys.bestFor: Casual players and kids who want laughs more than competition.
pros: Easy to pick up and very funny
Rounds take a minute or two
cons: Lots of ads and offers between rounds
body: Stumble Guys is an obstacle-course party game: everyone races through spinning hammers and collapsing floors, and only some players qualify for each next round.
It's light fun rather than a deep game, and that's the point. Expect plenty of ads and skin offers in the free version.
Stumble-Guys.author: editors

Subway-Surfers.verdict: The classic endless runner: instant fun in short bursts, and it runs on almost any phone.
Subway-Surfers.bestFor: Anyone who wants a quick game for a commute or a waiting room.
pros: Regular World Tour updates with new cities
cons: Little depth after the first few hours
body: Swipe to dodge trains, roll under barriers and grab coins while a guard chases you. Subway Surfers has barely changed in years, and it doesn't need to.
It's a perfect time-filler. It won't hold your attention like a story game, but few games are as easy to pick up for two minutes.
Subway-Surfers.author: editors

Candy-Crush-Saga.verdict: The famous match-3 puzzle game: well made and endless, but designed to sell you extra moves.
Candy-Crush-Saga.bestFor: Casual puzzle fans who play a few levels a day.
cons: Some levels feel designed to make you buy boosters
body: Candy Crush asks you to swap candies to make rows of three or more, with each level setting a goal like clearing jelly or collecting ingredients.
It's the standard every match-3 game is measured against. Just be aware that the hardest levels push you towards buying extra moves; playing slowly and patiently costs nothing.
Candy-Crush-Saga.author: editors

Hill-Climb-Racing-2.verdict: Physics-based driving that's simple to learn and hard to master, now with online cups and team events.
Hill-Climb-Racing-2.bestFor: Players who enjoy tinkering with upgrades and beating friends' times.
pros: Lots of vehicles and tuning options
body: Lean forward, lean back, and try not to flip. Hill Climb Racing 2 builds on the original with online races, more vehicles and a team system.
It's free and fun for a long time, though progress later on is slow unless you pay or watch ads.
Hill-Climb-Racing-2.author: editors

Hill-Climb-Racing.verdict: The original physics driving game: simpler than the sequel and still a joy on any phone.
Hill-Climb-Racing.bestFor: Players with older phones or who prefer offline, solo play.
body: The first Hill Climb Racing is just you, a car and a hilly road. Go too fast and you flip; run out of fuel and it's over.
If your phone is older or you mostly play without internet, it's a better pick than the sequel.
Hill-Climb-Racing.author: editors

8-Ball-Pool.verdict: The most popular pool game on mobile, with real opponents and smooth aiming.
8-Ball-Pool.bestFor: Anyone who enjoys pool and quick head-to-head matches.
cons: Premium cues give paying players an edge
body: 8 Ball Pool does one thing well: online pool against real people. Aiming feels natural and matches are quick.
The economy revolves around coins bet on each match and cues that improve your shots. You can play happily for free, but be aware of how quickly coins can go.
8-Ball-Pool.author: editors

EA-SPORTS-FC-Mobile-Soccer.verdict: Licensed soccer with real clubs and players, built around collecting cards for your team.
EA-SPORTS-FC-Mobile-Soccer.bestFor: Football fans who enjoy building a dream squad.
cons: Team building is driven by card packs
body: EA SPORTS FC Mobile lets you play short matches and build a team from player cards earned in events or packs.
It's the best choice if licensed teams matter to you. Matches are simplified for mobile, and the game is more about collecting than pure football.
EA-SPORTS-FC-Mobile-Soccer.author: editors

eFootball.verdict: Konami's football game focuses more on on-pitch play, with realistic matches and online modes.
eFootball.bestFor: Players who care about match realism more than card collecting.
cons: Some modes take time to unlock
body: eFootball offers fuller matches than most mobile football games, with detailed player movement and tactics.
If you want football that feels like a console game, it's the better pick; just make sure your phone has room for it.
eFootball.author: editors

Plants-vs-Zombies-2.verdict: A charming tower defense game that's easy for newcomers, with lots of free content.
pros: Many worlds and plants to unlock
cons: Some plants are locked behind purchases
body: Plant sunflowers for energy, then peashooters and other plants to stop waves of zombies crossing your lawn. Plants vs Zombies 2 takes the idea through many themed worlds.
It's a great first strategy game for kids and casual players. Purchases speed things up but aren't needed to finish most of it.
Plants-vs-Zombies-2.author: editors

Five-Nights-at-Freddys.verdict: The small horror game that started a phenomenon: tense, simple and very effective.
Five-Nights-at-Freddys.bestFor: Teens and adults who like jump scares.
cons: Very limited gameplay by modern standards
body: You're a night guard watching cameras, and the animatronic characters move when you're not looking. Manage doors and power until 6 a.m.
It's short and basic, but its tension still works. Rated Teen, and not for younger kids.
Five-Nights-at-Freddys.author: editors

Shadow-Fight-2-Special-Edition.verdict: The paid edition of a popular fighting game, without the ads and energy limits of the free version.
Shadow-Fight-2-Special-Edition.bestFor: Fighting game fans who want to play without interruptions.
pros: No ads and no energy timer
body: Shadow Fight 2 is a side-on fighting game with silhouette characters and a big range of weapons. The Special Edition removes the ads and the energy limit that slowed down the free version.
If you like fighting games, this is the way to play it.
Shadow-Fight-2-Special-Edition.author: editors

Jetpack-Joyride.verdict: A classic one-thumb runner with a great sense of humor and lots of gadgets.
Jetpack-Joyride.bestFor: Anyone who wants quick, light fun.
cons: Ads and offers in the free version
body: Hold to fly, release to fall. Jetpack Joyride is about dodging lasers and missiles while collecting coins, with wild vehicles to pick up along the way.
It's still one of the best games for a two-minute break.
Jetpack-Joyride.author: editors

Water-Sort-Puz---Color-Game.verdict: A relaxing sorting puzzle that's easy to play anywhere.
Water-Sort-Puz---Color-Game.bestFor: Players who want something calm and simple.
cons: Many ads in the free version
body: Pour colored water between tubes until each tube holds one color. That's the whole game, and it's surprisingly soothing.
It's perfect for short breaks, though the free version shows a lot of ads.
Water-Sort-Puz---Color-Game.author: editors

Match-Factory.verdict: A tidy 3D matching puzzle: find three of the same object in a pile and clear the board.
Match-Factory.bestFor: Puzzle fans who like a satisfying, quick-to-play game.
cons: Harder levels nudge you towards boosters
Timer adds pressure on later levels
body: Match Factory fills the screen with a jumble of 3D objects. Tap matching items in threes before your tray fills up.
It's simple and polished. Like many puzzle games, later levels lean on boosters.
Match-Factory.author: editors

Gardenscapes.verdict: A match-3 puzzle game with a garden to restore and a story to follow.
Gardenscapes.bestFor: Casual puzzle fans who like decorating and a light story.
body: Solve match-3 levels to earn stars, then spend them restoring a big garden with Austin the butler.
If you enjoy match-3 games and want a reason to keep going, the garden story is a nice extra.
Gardenscapes.author: editors

Mario-Kart-Tour.verdict: Mario Kart on phones, with easy controls but a lot of pressure to spend.
Mario-Kart-Tour.bestFor: Nintendo fans who want quick kart races.
pros: Familiar Mario Kart characters and tracks
body: Mario Kart Tour brings the series to phones with simplified controls and tracks inspired by real cities.
It's fun in short bursts, but the shop and passes are heavy for a Mario game.
Mario-Kart-Tour.author: editors

Traffic-Rider.verdict: A first-person motorbike game that feels fast and focused, and it can be played offline.
Traffic-Rider.bestFor: Players who like speed and simple goals.
body: Weave through traffic on a motorbike, seen from the rider's seat. Traffic Rider is about speed, near misses and upgrading bikes.
It's straightforward and fun, and doesn't need an internet connection.
Traffic-Rider.author: editors

Sudoku-Ultimate-Offline-puzzle.verdict: A clean, ad-free sudoku app with offline play.
Sudoku-Ultimate-Offline-puzzle.bestFor: Sudoku fans who want a simple app without distractions.
cons: Fewer extras than free sudoku apps
body: Sudoku Ultimate is a straightforward sudoku app: pick a difficulty and solve.
If you play sudoku daily, paying once for an ad-free app is worth it.
Sudoku-Ultimate-Offline-puzzle.author: editors

Toca-Life-World-Build-a-Story.verdict: A digital dollhouse where kids create their own stories, without scores, timers or failure.
Toca-Life-World-Build-a-Story.bestFor: Children aged roughly 6 to 12 who like pretend play.
cons: Little structure for kids who want goals
body: Toca Life World lets kids explore towns full of characters and objects and make up their own stories.
The free version has plenty to play with; extra locations are sold separately. Parents should check purchase settings.
Toca-Life-World-Build-a-Story.author: editors

Poly-Bridge-3.verdict: A physics puzzle game about building bridges, with a satisfying mix of engineering and comedy.
Poly-Bridge-3.bestFor: Puzzle fans who like problem-solving and experimenting.
body: Build a bridge with a limited budget and watch vehicles try to cross. When it collapses, you learn something.
It's a great choice if you like engineering puzzles. A tablet makes building easier.
Poly-Bridge-3.author: editors

Grand-Theft-Auto-San-Andreas.verdict: The classic open-world game on mobile: huge, story-rich and rated for adults.
Grand-Theft-Auto-San-Andreas.bestFor: Adults who want a big open world on their phone.
cons: Touch controls are clumsy in combat
body: GTA San Andreas brings the full open-world game to phones, with a big map and a long story.
It's rated Mature. Touch controls make shooting and driving harder than on consoles; a controller helps.
Grand-Theft-Auto-San-Andreas.author: editors

Earn-to-Die.verdict: A short, cheap zombie-driving game about upgrading your car to reach the end.
Earn-to-Die.bestFor: Players who enjoy simple upgrade loops.
body: Drive through zombies, earn money, upgrade, try again. Earn to Die is a simple loop that's very satisfying.
It's a small game, but it's cheap and complete.
Earn-to-Die.author: editors

Stickman-Hook.verdict: A simple swinging game that feels great with one tap.
Stickman-Hook.bestFor: Players who want quick, light fun.
body: Tap to grab hooks and swing a stickman through levels. It's easy to play and hard to stop.
It's a light game with heavy ads, but very satisfying in short bursts.
Stickman-Hook.author: editors

We've favored complete games over ones that only run offline in a cut-down mode.

method: Torunex recommends mobile games you can download from Google Play. Our goal is simple: help you decide what's worth your time, money and storage space.

Each review gives a score out of 5 based on gameplay and depth, how fair the ads and in-app purchases are, how well it plays on typical phones, and how long it stays fun. Editor's Choice marks the games we'd recommend to almost anyone.

Ratings, installs, prices, age ratings and update dates come directly from Google Play and are refreshed daily. Game names, icons and screenshots belong to their publishers and are shown from Google Play.
Publishers don't pay for reviews or list placements. Download links go to the official Google Play page.
We revisit lists regularly and update scores when games change. If you spot something out of date, contact us.
